summary:
This page contains only code and a figure.

The last four lines of **listing 4.8** (started on p.136) set an x-tick at every epoch (`plt.xticks(epochs)`), label the y-axis `"Loss"`, add a legend and display the plot with `plt.show()`.

**Figure 4.4, "Training and validation loss"**, is the result. The dashed red training-loss curve starts around 0.56 at epoch 1 and falls monotonically, below 0.1 by epoch 7 and to almost 0 by epoch 20. The solid blue validation-loss curve starts lower (about 0.43), reaches its minimum of roughly 0.28 at epochs 3-4, and then rises steadily to about 0.58 by epoch 20. The two curves cross near epoch 2. (Values read from the plot; approximate.) The authors' interpretation follows on p.138: the validation metrics peak at the fourth epoch, after which the model is **overfitting**, learning representations specific to the training data.

**Listing 4.9** plots accuracy the same way: `plt.clf()` clears the figure (per the callout), then `history_dict["accuracy"]` and `history_dict["val_accuracy"]` are plotted as dashed red (`"Training acc"`) and solid blue (`"Validation acc"`) lines with the title `"[IMDB] Training and validation accuracy"`, epoch ticks, the y-label `"Accuracy"`, a legend and `plt.show()`. The resulting figure 4.5 appears on p.138.

concepts.name: Overfitting (as seen in figure 4.4)
concepts.definition: Continued improvement on training data accompanied by worsening performance on unseen data.
concepts.intuition: The model starts memorizing the 15,000 training reviews instead of learning sentiment cues that transfer.
concepts.technical: Training loss -> ~0 while validation loss rises from ~0.28 (epoch 3-4) to ~0.58 (epoch 20).
concepts.significance: Determines how long to train; p.138 retrains for four epochs.
concepts.misconception: A near-zero training loss is not a sign of a good model.

concepts.name: Learning curves
concepts.definition: Per-epoch plots of training and validation loss/metrics.
concepts.intuition: A dashboard showing whether more training still helps.
concepts.significance: The main tool for choosing the number of epochs.
concepts.misconception: Look at the validation curve, not the training curve, to choose the epoch.

deeper.title: Reading figure 4.4 step by step
deeper.body: AI reading of the figure: (1) Epochs 1-3: both losses drop; the model is learning general patterns. (2) Around epochs 3-4: validation loss is at its minimum (~0.28); this is the best model. (3) Epoch 5 onward: training loss keeps falling toward 0 but validation loss rises steadily; each further epoch fits training-specific noise. (4) At epoch 20, validation loss (~0.58) is about twice its minimum, so the final weights are clearly worse than those of epoch 4. The book's own interpretation is on p.138.

deeper.title: Why validation loss can rise even if accuracy barely changes
deeper.body: Beyond the book: crossentropy punishes confident mistakes heavily. An overfitting model becomes extremely confident (predictions near 0 or 1); the few validation reviews it gets wrong then incur very large losses, so validation loss can climb sharply while validation accuracy only drifts down slightly. Compare figure 4.4 with figure 4.5 on p.138.

questions.question: Around which epoch is the validation loss in figure 4.4 lowest?
questions.explanation: The blue curve bottoms out near 0.28 at epochs 3-4 (p.138 says the metrics peak at the fourth epoch). Epoch 1 is higher (~0.43); epochs 10 and 20 are higher still as validation loss climbs.

questions.question: What does the growing gap between the training and validation curves in figure 4.4 indicate?
questions.answer: Overfitting: the model keeps fitting the training data better while getting worse on unseen data.

questions.question: What does plt.clf() do at the start of listing 4.9 and why is it needed?
questions.answer: It clears the current figure so the accuracy curves are not drawn on top of the loss curves.

questions.question: Which History keys does listing 4.9 read?
If you had to pick a number of epochs from figure 4.4 alone, which is the most defensible?
questions.explanation: Epoch 4 is at the validation minimum; p.138 indeed retrains for four epochs. 1 underfits (higher validation loss); 12 and 20 overfit.

questions.question: Can you sketch, from memory, how the training and validation accuracy curves of figure 4.5 should look given figure 4.4?
questions.answer: Training accuracy rising toward 1; validation accuracy peaking around epoch 4 then flattening or slightly declining.
